title: Redwood - Constellation Cloud Marketplace Integration Sync
summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture artifacts, billing/integration touchpoints, and joint solution collateral. Action items include sharing reference architecture diagram, marketplace asset checklist, and a short pilot plan for private deployment testing.
next_steps: Redwood to send marketplace asset checklist and sample listing copy by 2026-12-15
Priya to share reference architecture diagram and terraform snippet by 2026-12-17
Constellation to provide test account + sample customer VPC details by 2026-12-20
Schedule follow-up demo for billing integration and entitlement flow week of 2026-12-21
action_items: Priya Desai (Redwood SE): draft reference architecture diagram and Terraform example - due 2026-12-17
Jordan Lee (Redwood AE): share marketplace asset checklist and sample listing copy - due 2026-12-15
Evan Park (Constellation PM): provision test account and sample VPC details - due 2026-12-20
Lina Ortiz (Constellation Eng): gather compliance doc links (SOC2/ISO) for listing - due 2026-12-18
Marco Alvarez (Redwood Solutions): run quick smoke test of private deployment with Constellation sample by 2026-12-22
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Jordan from Redwood, AE. we have Priya and Marco from the tech side. how's everybody doing?
[00:08] Evan Park: good, thanks. Evan here. excited to sync.
[00:12] Lina Ortiz: Lina on the marketplace engineering team, hey.
[00:15] Marco Alvarez: hey all. sorry for the slight delay, had a jira that was being... uh... resolved.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: no worries. quick agenda: marketplace listing reqs, reference arch and joint solution collateral, billing/integration flow, and next steps. feel free to jump in.
[00:28] Priya Desai: i'll kick off with architecture overview from the Redwood side then we can map to Constellation's marketplace requirements.
[00:33] Evan Park: sounds good.
[00:36] Priya Desai: so, quick recap — Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). for marketplace we usually see two paths: a managed listing that points to hosted endpoints or a private offering where we provide an AMI/container and the partner runs it in their cloud.
[00:55] Lina Ortiz: for Constellation we prefer marketplace listings that enable one-click deploy to a customer's VPC, but we also support SaaS listings. our ops team will want an image and terraform snippet.
[01:05] Priya Desai: right. we can provide a reference architecture diagram, terraform examples, and a hardened container. small caveat — for private deployments customers will want KMS integration and customer-managed keys, and we need to map how license/entitlement is passed from the marketplace to the runtime.
[01:21] Tom Miller: yeah entitlement mapping is big for us. do you have an example of how Redwood handles license tokens or marketplace entitlements?
[01:28] Jordan Lee: on the Redwood side we usually use a signed entitlement token that the runtime validates at boot, and for long-running private deployments we periodically refresh via the control plane. in dedicated/reserved setups we tie capacity to the contract and billing is outside marketplace, but for marketplace-led purchases we integrate with the partner's entitlement API.
[01:46] Priya Desai: quick note — the runtime can accept a marketplace token or a customer API key, and we have a small adapter library that validates signatures and exchanges for an internal session token. it's lightweight.
[01:56] Lina Ortiz: ok, can you share that adapter library? is it open source?
[01:59] Priya Desai: we can share a reference implementation (python + terraform example). not full OSS but a permissive snippet for partners.
[02:06] Evan Park: great. on the marketplace artifact side, we'll need: listing copy, logos, short and long descriptions, a 90-second demo video, architecture diagram, install instructions, and compliance docs (SOC 2/ISO). also pricing metadata.
[02:19] Jordan Lee: noted. we'll pull together the copy and assets. Marco, can you speak to observability/logs in private deployments? Constellation's customers will ask about audit logs.
[02:29] Marco Alvarez: yes. in private we can push logs to a customer-managed endpoint (splunk/elk/o11y endpoint) or keep logs local with audit exports to S3. we support KMS keys for encrypting logs at rest. there is minor config to flip on. also we emit structured metrics for per-route latency, token counts etc.
[02:47] Lina Ortiz: that's good. we need proof that audit logs can be exported to a Constellation account and that RBAC integrates with SSO.
[02:55] Priya Desai: for SSO we have SAML and OIDC integrations at the control plane level. for the runtime we support role-based clients that map to SAML groups. we can show mapping examples.
[03:07] Evan Park: timeline wise, our marketplace deadlines for Q1 listings: content freeze is 2027-01-20. we need the assets and a validated deploy workflow by then to make it.
[03:17] Jordan Lee: ok, that's tight but doable. we'll prioritize the asset checklist.
[03:21] Tom Miller: technical question — latency and model variants. some of our customers will care about lowest-latency variants. can Redwood's marketplace listing allow specifying pinned model versions or variants (e.g., quantized)?
[03:33] Priya Desai: yes, the listing can document supported model variants. for hosted we provide performance profiles; for private we include recommended quantized builds and instructions for selecting the right bin. small warning: some kernels behave differently on older hardware so we recommend specific instance types.
[03:50] Lina Ortiz: instance types doc would be helpful.
[03:52] Marco Alvarez: we'll include an instance compatibility matrix in the ref arch doc.
[03:56] Evan Park: another ask: billing integration. our marketplace pushes a purchase event and issues an entitlement. how does Redwood handle metering for usage-based billing?
[04:06] Jordan Lee: for hosted API purchases via marketplace we map purchases to accounts and we emit usage reports per customer. we can either accept marketplace billing (where Constellation bills the customer) or we can bill directly and the marketplace handles license pass-through depending on the integration type.
[04:23] Priya Desai: for usage metering in private deployments we can ship an agent that reports aggregated token counts and usage metrics to the partner's entitlement service. privacy note: payloads can be aggregated and only include counters, not PII or content.
[04:37] Tom Miller: ok good. is that agent open to network restrictions? some enterprise customers are air-gapped.
[04:42] Priya Desai: yes, we have an offline reporting mode where the agent writes daily summaries to a bucket that partner ops pulls. no outbound required.
[04:50] Evan Park: perfect.
[04:52] [05:00] Jordan Lee: quick clarification — does Constellation want Redwood to publish the listing, or will Constellation publish and Redwood provides the assets?
[05:08] Lina Ortiz: we prefer partner-published listings so partner controls the storefront. but we can co-publish in some cases.
[05:14] Jordan Lee: okay we'll prepare the assets in a partner-friendly format (zipped assets, markdown sample listing).
[05:19] Marco Alvarez: technical deep dive: i wanted to call out compatibility for private deployments — we tested our runtime on K8s and on single-node container deployments. for marketplace we can provide a helm chart and a plain container/compose example.
[05:33] Lina Ortiz: helm chart required for our one-click deploy. terraform alone isn't sufficient.
[05:38] Priya Desai: understood. we'll include helm charts and a quick-start helm values file pre-populated for Constellation.
[05:45] Evan Park: security review — will Redwood provide SOC2 or ISO artifacts? we need attestations for the listing.
[05:52] Jordan Lee: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 summaries and we can provide a short package of redacted reports and a security whitepaper.
[06:00] Tom Miller: can you include a data flow diagram that shows where data leaves the customer's VPC, if at all? that's a checklist item for our compliance team.
[06:08] Priya Desai: we'll include that in the ref arch doc and highlight optional flows: fully in-VPC (no egress), egress to partner-managed control plane, and hybrid. we'll also mark the KMS boundary.
[06:21] Evan Park: excellent.
[06:23] [06:30] Jordan Lee: switching to release and QA: marketplace will expect a validated install workflow. can we run a pilot with one of your internal accounts?
[06:39] Evan Park: yes. i'll provision a sandbox account and send creds. expect some constraints on IP whitelisting.
[06:45] Priya Desai: fine. for the pilot we'll do a 1-2 day smoke test: deploy via helm, run a basic inference job, validate logging and entitlement checks, and exercise metering.
[06:58] Lina Ortiz: timeline for pilot?
[07:01] Jordan Lee: suggest week of 2026-12-27 to align with your holidays padded schedule.
[07:07] Evan Park: works for us.
[07:09] Tom Miller: one more technical: what's the KV cache behavior in private vs hosted? some customers rely on warmed caches for low latency.
[07:18] Priya Desai: in hosted mode we have shared caching at the runtime level and prefix caching to speed repeated prompts. in private mode the cache is local to the instance and can be persisted based on config. for very low-latency we support a small in-memory warmup and can seed cache from a snapshot. note: seeding caches requires sharing masked prompts so watch out for PII.
[07:37] Marco Alvarez: also note quantized model variants have different KV cache morphology; there's a minor perf delta. we'll document it.
[07:45] Evan Park: good to know.
[07:47] [08:00] Jordan Lee: logistic Q — bundle or metered listing? Constellation, do you plan to support per-seat/per-month pricing or usage-based metering?
[08:09] Evan Park: our marketplace supports both. most ISVs start with subscription + overage. we'd like to support usage metering if Redwood can emit daily usage files.
[08:18] Priya Desai: we can emit daily metering files to a Constellation S3, or push to your entitlement API. we'll provide both patterns.
[08:27] Lina Ortiz: S3 drop is simplest for now.
[08:30] Jordan Lee: ok S3 drop and API push both documented.
[08:34] [08:45] Tom Miller: curious about rollback and upgrades. if a customer upgrades the model version via marketplace how do we ensure compatibility?
[08:53] Priya Desai: we recommend semantic versioning and a canary rollout pattern. our deployment tooling supports A/B of model variants and automatic fallback to last known-good. we'll supply helm hooks that perform canary validation.
[09:05] Evan Park: we'll need those helm hooks in the example repo.
[09:08] Marco Alvarez: noted.
[09:10] [09:30] Jordan Lee: a couple of small items — logos specs and video length? Constellation asked for 90-second demo. any brand constraints?
[09:18] Lina Ortiz: logos 1024x1024 png and svg ideally. demo 90-120 seconds mp4 H.264. keep it short.
[09:25] Jordan Lee: thank you. we'll produce.
[09:29] Evan Park: regarding partner support — will Redwood provide a support SLA TIER for listings?
[09:35] Jordan Lee: yes we have partner SLAs; for listings we usually offer a 24/5 L2 support during pilot and can extend to enterprise SLA for GA.
[09:44] Priya Desai: also to note: our release artifacts include a smoke test script that customers can run post-deploy, we'll share that.
[09:52] [10:00] Tom Miller: back to compliance — does Redwood support customer-managed KMS (HSM) integration? some finance customers require HSM-backed keys.
[10:09] Marco Alvarez: yes we support customer-managed KMS and can optionally call out HSM if the partner supports. we have a KMS plugin for major cloud KMS providers.
[10:19] Evan Park: good.
[10:21] [10:30] Jordan Lee: i want to surface a small risk — some older instance types have suboptimal AVX support and quantized kernels might fallback to slower code paths. we'll mark recommended instance families in the doc.
[10:43] Priya Desai: and we'll include perf numbers for common sequence lengths so Constellation can include realistic latency expectations in the listing.
[10:51] Lina Ortiz: those perf numbers are critical for enterprise shoppers.
[10:55] Evan Park: agreed.
[10:58] [11:00] Jordan Lee: okay, any other questions from Constellation?
[11:02] Lina Ortiz: nothing immediate. one request: can you provide a short reference customer case (redacted) for a similar marketplace listing? helps our reviewers.
[11:12] Jordan Lee: yes we can provide a short one-page case study with redacted logos and metrics.
[11:17] Tom Miller: perfect.
[11:19] [11:30] Priya Desai: i'll summarize technical deliverables: ref arch diagram, helm chart, terraform snippet, adapter library for entitlements, agent for metering, instance compatibility matrix, perf numbers, smoke test scripts, and example helm hooks for canary.
[11:43] Evan Park: that's great.
[11:45] Jordan Lee: recap next steps: Jordan to send asset checklist, Priya to share ref arch and code samples, Constellation to provision sandbox. we'll schedule the pilot last week of Dec.
[11:58] Marco Alvarez: small note: i'll open a shared repo and give Constellation read access today. that repo will have a draft helm chart and smoke tests.
[12:07] Evan Park: awesome, thanks Marco.
[12:10] Lina Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[12:12] Jordan Lee: thanks all. we'll follow up via email with links and dates. bye.
[12:16] [End of recording]
